title: real-time-attn-prefetch-fusion-rotary-lazy-commit
author: Nikhil Rao
description: Motivation: reduce tail latency for mixed short/long requests and lower per-token CPU/GPU overhead by combining a lightweight prefetching path with a deferred (lazy) KV cache commit. This PR introduces a real-time attention prefetch+fusion path that coalesces rotary parameter application, QK fusion, and an interleaved KV prefetch stage. The lazy-commit mechanism defers writing to the global KV cache until an amortized threshold is hit, avoiding frequent small writes that stall the serving pipeline. This is targeted at continuous-batching workloads where short requests interleave with long-context streams. The change includes a scheduler hint that prioritizes in-flight prefix KV reads, a new fused kernel for rotary+qk microfusion (fallbacks to existing Flash-compatible kernels), and telemetry hooks for per-request cache hit/miss accounting. The description below contains implementation summary, commits, high-level files changed, benchmark summary, review thread highlights, CI summary, and merge notes.

review_comments: Aisha Gomez: Can you add memory-safety checks for deferred KV frames? Observed earlier leaks with partial evictions.
Nikhil Rao: Added boundary checks and a short-running valgrind-style test in test_lazy_commit.py; see new test case 'test_partial_eviction_safety'.
Tom Fletcher: Benchmarks look promising. Please include p50/p95/p99 numbers across 1/4/16 concurrent connections and a long-context stress test.

Evan Liu: We need deterministic fallback to the old flash path when the microfusion kernel reports an unsupported configuration. Ensure the dispatcher sets the kernel flag atomically to avoid race conditions.
Nikhil Rao: Dispatcher updated to use the runtime kernel registry with atomic switches; added unit to simulate concurrent registration.
Tom Fletcher: Minor: move the config knob to runtime flags and not a compile-time macro so ops teams can toggle safely in prod without rebuilds.
Nikhil Rao: Moved tunables to runtime config; documented the flags in docs/perf/real_time_prefetch.md.
Aisha Gomez: LGTM after CI green and a short post-merge canary on dedicated clusters.
bench_results: Mixed workload (50% short requests < 40 tokens, 50% long requests 2048 tokens) on T4-like instance: overall token throughput +18% and p95 latency -12% compared to main baseline
Short-only workload (1-10 tokens): p50 latency -22%, p95 -15%
Long-only workload (2048 tokens): throughput +6%, p99 latency unchanged
Continuous-batching scenario: per-token GPU utilization reduced 9% and host CPU spin reduced 14% due to amortized KV writes
release_notes: Introduce a real-time prefetch+fusion attention path with lazy KV commit to improve mixed-workload tail latency and reduce per-token cost. Can be toggled via runtime config: runtime.attn.prefetch.enabled and runtime.kv.lazy_commit.threshold.
